title: Sigillatim vs in seed — OT proves Gospel in genere
source_text: XI. Praeterea dogmata quaedam ex aliquo principio deduci possunt duobus modis. Primo sigillatim, distincte & per se. Deinde generatim confuse, & per aliud. Sic omnia religionis Christianae dogmata & instituta ex Scriptura veteris Testamenti probari non possunt per se & sigillatim. Ut, exempli gratia, fideles esse baptizandos in Nomine Patris, Filii, & Spiritus sancti ex veteri Testamento satis probari non posset, si nullum aliud fidei principium suppeteret praeter illam veterem Scripturam. Et tamen omnia quae ad Evangelicam doctrinam pertinent ex veteri Testamento in genere probari possunt, quatenus inde potest efficaciter demonstrari Jesum Nazarenum esse Messiam, & Dei Filium a Prophetis promissum: adeoque doctrinam illius veram & divinam esse, & ejus instituta tanquam divina a nobis amplectenda. Quae generatim & confuse tantum ex aliquo principio colligi, & deduci possunt, in eo continentur virtute atque in semine. Quae vero ex eo probantur distincte & sigillatim expresse dici possunt aliquo modo in eo contineri: licet strictiori sensu expresse idem significet ac diserte & immediate.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, certain dogmas can be deduced from some principle in two ways. First sigillatim, distinctly and by themselves. Then generally in a confused way, and through another. Thus all dogmas and institutions of the Christian religion cannot be proved from the Scripture of the Old Testament by themselves and sigillatim. As, for example, that the faithful are to be baptized in the Name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit could not be sufficiently proved from the Old Testament, if no other principle of faith were at hand besides that old Scripture. And yet all things which pertain to Evangelic doctrine can be proved from the Old Testament in genere, insofar as from it it can be efficaciously demonstrated that Jesus the Nazarene is the Messiah, and the Son of God promised by the Prophets: and therefore that his doctrine is true and divine, and that his institutions are to be embraced by us as divine. Those things which can only be gathered and deduced from some principle generally and confusedly are contained in it by virtue and in seed. But those which are proved from it distinctly and sigillatim can be said to be contained in it expressly in some way: although in a stricter sense 'expressly' signifies the same as clearly and immediately.
pass_b_english: Dogmas may also be drawn from a principle in two ways: item by item, distinctly and of themselves; or only in a general, mixed way, through something else.

Not every Christian dogma and ordinance can be proved from the Old Testament by itself, one by one. Baptism in the Name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit could not be shown from the Old Testament alone if that were our only principle of faith.

Yet everything that belongs to Gospel teaching can be proved from the Old Testament in general, because from it one can show effectively that Jesus of Nazareth is the Messiah and the Son of God promised by the Prophets — and therefore that his teaching is true and divine, and his ordinances to be received as divine.

What follows from a principle only in that general, mixed way is in it by force and in seed. What is proved from it distinctly, item by item, may be said to be in it expressly in a looser sense — though strictly 'expressly' means the same as clearly and immediately.

lemmas.gloss: item by item / one by one
generally in a confused / mixed way

choices.why: Le Blanc pairs with distincte and per se against confuse.
